Here's some inline math:

$e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$

And display math:

$$
p(y \mid x)
=
\frac{p(x \mid y)p(y)}{p(x)}
$$

## Python
  ```{python}
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
x = rng.normal(size=1000)

x.mean(), x.std()
```

## Plot

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.hist(x, bins=30)
ax.set_title("Normally distributed things")
plt.show()
```
